title: P-5-P conversion: chemical mass versus biological response

content.summary: Chemical mass equivalence, declared vitamin B6 amount, absorption and clinical dose equivalence are different concepts. No universal P-5-P-to-pyridoxine biological potency ratio or percentage converted to usable B6 is established by this reference review.
content.metabolism: Phosphorylated B6 forms undergo dephosphorylation before intestinal absorption; absorbed forms can be phosphorylated again. Active coenzyme identity does not mean oral P-5-P bypasses all metabolism.
content.chemical_calculation: For educational equimolar comparisons only: compound mass multiplied by pyridoxine molecular weight divided by source-compound molecular weight gives an equimolar pyridoxine mass. This is not an absorption, retained-dose, clinical-effect, safety or universal regulatory labeling conversion.
content.chemical_assumptions: Calculations assume pure, correctly identified compounds and exactly the specified hydration state. Unknown salts, variable hydrates, mixtures, assays or excipients invalidate a simple application. Do not use molecular weight alone to assign a scanned product’s nutrient amount.
content.declared_amount: When a label declares Vitamin B6 X mg (as pyridoxal 5-phosphate), X is the stated nutrient amount; do not automatically discount it again using a compound-mass factor. A separate statement of raw P-5-P compound mass is not the same field. Confirm jurisdiction, label basis, actual chemical form and manufacturer documentation before any reconciliation.
content.biological_boundary: Molar ratios do not establish that a given P-5-P dose produces the same blood concentration, tissue effect, therapeutic benefit or neuropathy risk as a pyridoxine dose. Do not supply a personal switching formula or infer that P-5-P is safer.
content.evidence_boundary: Diet-versus-synthetic B6 availability assumptions and urinary recovery percentages are not P-5-P-to-pyridoxine potency conversion rates. They must not be repurposed into such a calculator.
content.dose_notice: All numerical examples are chemical illustrations, not doses to take, safety thresholds or substitutions.

integration_guards: Educational comparisons only; no automatic nutrient-total conversion.
Do not reinterpret an already declared B6 nutrient amount as raw compound mass.
Do not apply anhydrous factors to monohydrates, other salts or unknown hydrates.
Do not infer absorption percentages or clinical potency from molecular weights.
Keep B6 neuropathy warnings and US/EFSA reference-context distinctions from the main batch.
